subject: Clarify: rounding behaviour for streaming tokens + long-context split
messages:
From: Emma Collins <emma@finlytics.com>

Subject: Question: rounding & long-context split for streaming billing

Hi Jonas,

Quick question from the FinLytics billing team as we test the streaming integration: we captured a sample of ~3000 streaming responses across a day and want to make sure we understand how Redwood will bill these. Attached is finlytics_sample_trace.csv with per-request token counts and whether we used continuous streaming or request/response.

Three things we're unclear on:
1) If a streaming response yields 47 tokens in a micro-burst and streaming chunking emits two internal write events (30 + 17), do you round each write to your billing quantum or the full response token count?
2) For a single conversational session where the active context grows past the 16k band and we transparently fall back to a 32k context model variant mid-session, how is the context length billed for that session slice?
3) Do you apply any per-call minimum when the prompt+response is < 10 tokens (we have lots of short status pings)?

If you can point to the exact rules (or example math) we'd appreciate it — the accounting team needs examples to reconcile their pilot invoice. Happy to hop on a 30-min call if it's easier.

Thanks,
Emma Collins
Head of Platform Integrations
FinLytics

From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Question: rounding & long-context split for streaming billing

Emma — thanks for the trace, that helped. High-level answers first, then I'll include two worked examples: one for streaming micro-bursts and one for a model-variant fallthrough.

Short answers:
- We bill on the logical request/response token accounting, not intermediate OS-level write chunks. So a 47-token response billed as 47 tokens (subject to quantum rounding described below).
- If we swap to a larger context model mid-session, we bill each inference call by the model variant that served that call. Context-length contribution is per call; we don't retroactively reclassify prior calls.
- There is a per-request minimum equivalent to 5 tokens for hosted tiers (this is small and intended to prevent extreme micro-requests). Dedicated customers can request a lower floor in contracts.

I'll attach a short workbook with two examples. Quick caveat: billed "token units" are then bucketed into the customer's pricing slab and min-rounding quantum (our default is 8-token quantum for metering) — that rounding happens at the invoice line-item stage after the per-call aggregation.

Worked examples (abbreviated):
A) Streaming micro-burst: client emits two writes (30 + 17) but the runtime presents those as one logical response = 47 tokens billed. Rounding: we apply the 8-token quantum to the aggregated 47 -> round up to nearest multiple = 48 tokens billed.
B) Model fallthrough: session calls: Call 1 (12k context, model-x, billed at model-x per-call), Call 2 (17k context, model-y after fallthrough) -> we bill Call 1 at model-x rates with its token counts, Call 2 at model-y rates. We do not merge the two calls for rounding; each call is rounded separately to the quantum.

Next steps: Sergio — can you add the per-call arithmetic in a reply so Emma's team can copy/paste the table? Grace — I flagged Dedicated-floor concession as negotiable on the deal; can we prep a short note for Emma about lowering the per-request minimum if they push for it?

Thanks,

Subject: Re: Question: rounding & long-context split for streaming billing

Emma / team — adding concrete rows you can paste into your reconciliation sheet. I used the default 8-token quantum and the 5-token per-call minimum that Jonas mentioned. All math below is tokens -> quantum rounding -> billed tokens; final pricing depends on model SKU.

Example 1: micro-burst single logical response- raw response tokens: 47- quantum: 8 tokens- rounded billed units = ceil(47 / 8) * 8 = ceil(5.875) * 8 = 6 * 8 = 48 billed tokens

Example 2: micro-pings sequence (three calls in one minute)- call A: 3 tokens -> apply per-call minimum 5 -> rounded to quantum: ceil(5 / 8) * 8 = 8 billed tokens- call B: 2 tokens -> minimum 5 -> rounded -> 8 billed tokens- call C: 9 tokens -> no minimum applied beyond 5 -> rounded: ceil(9 / 8) * 8 = 16 billed tokens- aggregate billed tokens for minute = 8 + 8 + 16 = 32

Example 3: model fallthrough within a session- call 1: context 12,400 tokens, model-x per-token = A- call 2: context 17,200 tokens, model-y per-token = B- billing: call1 billed at model-x rate for its token counts (rounded per-call), call2 billed at model-y rate (rounded per-call). No reclassification or retroactive charging for earlier calls.

Notes:
- For customers worried about repetitive ultra-short pings we recommend client-side batching or a short debounce (100–200ms) so multiple tiny pings collapse into one logical call. That reduces quantum losses.
- For Dedicated customers we can: (a) lower the quantum, (b) set a different per-call minimum, or (c) offer a blended commit that amortizes microcalls.

Happy to share a CSV of the above calculations against your trace; if you want that, send the trace subset (or confirm the rows you care about).

—Sergio
